roof_form.note: EXTENDS TEST 1 — PASSED, with a caveat about ordering. In 0.1.0 I had to restate the whole variants list to say 'the parent's second choice is my first'. Two op:replace records now do it. The caveat is that preference order is being carried by the canonical/permitted STATUS rather than by position, so the schema gives three levels of preference and no more; that is enough here and would not be enough for a style with five ranked roof forms. Nothing else about the slot is restated: the hip ridge ratio, the six forbidden forms and the rule all inherit.

roof_pitch.rule: Rise:run between 7:12 and 9:12 — a full step shallower than the New England band, and the reason a Virginia house reads lower at the same width.
roof_pitch.note: Specified rather than extends on purpose. The parent's four region-scoped pitch parameters would all merge through and sit alongside these, which is noise: a resolved Tidewater kit should not still be carrying pitch_new_england. This is a case where extends is available and wrong.

variants.note: A New England device and climatically wrong here: it keeps the stack's stored heat inside the envelope, which is the opposite of what a Chesapeake summer wants.
The tall paired stacks joined above the roof by an arched brick curtain are visible from a mile away and are conclusive against New England.

height_above_ridge_min.note: Not less than 6 ft clear of the ridge, against the parent's 24 in floor.

chimney.note: EXTENDS TEST 2 — PASSED CLEANLY, and this is the case that most needed it. The parent states the invariant (paired, symmetrical, never a single central stack, plan dimensions in whole bricks) and that invariant is still true here; only the gable-to-ridge position changes. In 0.1.0 I restated the count, the pairing rule and the whole-brick stack plan in order to move the chimneys sideways, and every one of those restatements was a copy that would go stale. This file now says nothing it inherits.

variants.note: 13.5 in of brick with a real through-bond, which is what makes the Flemish bond and the 4-8 in reveal physically possible.

exterior_architrave.note: The wall's depth is the window's only surround, and the austerity that follows is a large part of why a Virginia front looks unlike a Massachusetts one at the same size.

reveal_frame.rule: As georgian-colonial-american: a frame opening sits nearly flush.
reveal_frame.note: OQ 19, 24 Aug 2026. This slot was a verbatim copy of `reveal_masonry` and therefore stated the MASONRY answer under the frame id: a 13.5 in wall, a 4 to 8 in reveal and no exterior architrave. A frame Tidewater house would have been drawn with a brick wall's reveal. It now extends the parent, which carries the real frame answer (5 to 7 in wall, under 2 in of reveal, depth given by the architrave), and states nothing of its own -- because nothing in this corpus sources a Tidewater DEPARTURE from that, and inventing one to fill the slot is what the copy already did once.

arch.rule: Segmental with a rise of one eighth of the opening before about 1750, flat and cambered after -- the date of the house is readable off the rise.
arch.note: Moved here from `window_head_masonry` 24 Aug 2026 (OQ 46). SPLIT 24 Aug 2026 (OQ 46). This slot carried two different claims at once: how the top of a masonry window is BUILT -- gauged and rubbed brick, one head datum a storey, an architrave, a keystone or its absence -- and the GEOMETRY of the arch doing the spanning. The second has moved to the `arch` slot and this slot names it in `determined_by`, which is the mechanism OQ 19 built for exactly this: a slot decided by another names it rather than restating its numbers.

entry_sequence.note: A case the schema handles better than I expected. The child does not contradict the parent at all; it changes what the parent's rule is FOR — phenomenological in the parent, mechanical here. Adding one parameter and a note now carries that, where 0.1.0 forced a full restatement of a rule I agreed with.

first_floor.note: A foot to eighteen inches taller than the parent's Northern-weighted band. Stack effect, not status.

ceiling_height_rule.note: EXTENDS TEST 3 — PASSED CLEANLY. Only two numbers change. The rule ('snapped to a whole number of brick courses before anything else is set out'), the four regional parameters, the attic band and the three-pack precedence order all inherit untouched. In 0.1.0 this slot restated the rule and both pack derivations to change two ranges. AND THE RESOLVER CAUGHT ME OVERCLAIMING HERE, which is worth recording. I first wrote that at a 132 in ceiling trim-classical's nineteenth-part derivation comes back into calibration. It does not, quite: 132 x 4/19 is 27.8 in, still two inches under the measured 30-32 band. The derivation only reaches 30 in at a 142.5 in ceiling. So the pack's own stated calibration range of 11-13 ft is itself about a foot too generous at the bottom, and even a Tidewater room needs to be at the TOP of this variant's band before the pure derivation agrees with the tape measure. The in_calibration flag inherited from the parent is therefore still correctly false at 132 in, and the resolver's stale-calibration warning is what surfaced the error.

variants.note: A side hall does not ventilate.

doors_at_both_ends.note: Both operable, aligned on axis. The passage is a ventilation device before it is a hallway.

min_passage_width.note: Narrowing below 9 ft defeats it. A hard floor the parent does not have.

Dutch and French colonial. A corner hearth has no chimney position on a gable-end stack.

hearth_position.rule: Hearths are at the gable ends, on the outside walls of the end rooms, so the mass of the stack sits outside the heated volume in summer.
hearth_position.note: Kept separate from `chimney` because the ontology separates the roof expression from the plan fact. Here they are one decision that happens to agree, and the two slots therefore say the same thing twice — the one duplication in this file I could not remove, because `determined_by` runs one way and there is no way to say 'these two slots are the same decision'.

opposed_openings_required.note: Stronger than the parent's 'windows on two walls': in a single-pile plan the two walls are OPPOSITE, which is what makes the draft cross.

variants.note: The best answer where the composition is five-part: the plant goes wholly outside the main block, in the dependency the style already uses for the noisy and the dangerous.

services_strategy.note: Included to test extends on one of the invented slots. It works, and it exposes something: the parent's `invented: true` flag inherits, which is correct, but there is no way for this file to record that it is extending an invention rather than a retrieval — the provenance of the DELTA is not tracked separately from the provenance of the slot.

preferred_passage_axis.value: within 45 degrees of the prevailing summer breeze where the approach permits
preferred_passage_axis.note: A SECOND criterion, subordinate to the approach. The parent's rule that orientation follows the approach and not the sun is still true and is not restated.

two_show_fronts.value: land front and river front, both fully composed

orientation_rule.note: EXTENDS TEST 4 — PARTIAL, AND THIS IS THE ONE RESIDUAL FAILURE. The parameter half works exactly as asked: the secondary criterion is added and the parent's governing_factor is inherited without a copy. The prose half does not. `rule` is a single string with no merge operator, so a child that wants to ADD a clause to an inherited sentence must either replace the whole sentence or, as here, leave the rule inherited and let the delta live only in a parameter — which means the resolved rule sentence still reads 'the house is oriented to its approach and to symmetry' and never mentions the breeze. I chose the second because a stale copy is worse than an incomplete sentence, but neither is right. `rule` wants either an append operator or a companion `rule_addendum` field.

variants.note: The Tidewater house sits low. Charleston raises the principal floor a full storey on an arcaded basement, which is one of the largest differences between the two Southern variants and would otherwise be invisible in the resolved kit.
